Where public leaders
learn to lead.
settings.copy: For nearly a century, the Fenwick School has trained the people who shape public life. Our graduate programs in public policy, public administration, and data-driven governance combine academic rigor with the practical work of building better institutions.

trust_list.text: Ranked in the top 20 public-affairs schools nationally
1,200+ alumni in public service across 14 countries
90% of graduates placed within six months

stats.label: Alumni serving in public roles worldwide
Core faculty across four academic tracks

settings.title: Programs built for
settings.intro: Four graduate programs, one mission: to give you the analytical tools, ethical grounding, and hands-on experience to lead in public life.

features.title: Master of Public Policy
features.text: A two-year, data-intensive program in economic analysis, policy evaluation, and program design. Ideal for analysts and advisors who want to shape what governments do.

features.title: Master of Public Administration
features.text: For managers and executives in the public and nonprofit sectors. Focused on organizational leadership, budgeting, and the craft of running public institutions well.

features.title: MS in Data & Governance
features.text: The newest track — where statistics meets public decision-making. Learn to build the models and evidence base that modern agencies rely on.

features.title: PhD in Public Affairs
features.text: A research-intensive doctorate for future scholars and policy researchers. Funded for five years, with mentorship from our leading faculty.

settings.title: Learning that
settings.intro: The classroom is only half the education. Every Fenwick student leaves campus with a portfolio of real policy work, not just a transcript.

steps.title: Learn the craft
steps.text: Core seminars in economics, law, statistics, and public management build the shared foundation every public leader needs.

steps.title: Apply it live
steps.text: Capstone clients are real agencies — city halls, nonprofits, and legislative offices — that commission our students' analysis and take the recommendations seriously.

steps.title: Learn from practice
steps.text: Practitioner-in-residence programs bring working officials, analysts, and advocates into the classroom every week.

steps.title: Launch your career
steps.text: Our placement office and 1,200-strong alumni network open doors in government, NGOs, and the public sector's growing data roles.

settings.note: Last year alone, Fenwick capstone teams delivered 31 policy memos to partner agencies — 12 of which were adopted.

settings.title: Questions prospective
settings.intro: Everything you need to know about applying to the Fenwick School — from requirements to funding.

items.question: What do I need to apply?
items.answer: A bachelor's degree, a personal statement, two letters of recommendation, and — for most tracks — GRE scores. We review applications holistically; professional experience matters as much as your transcript.

items.question: Is financial support available?
items.answer: Yes. 94% of our graduate students receive some form of funding — from merit scholarships to research assistantships and paid capstone fellowships. We are committed to making public service careers financially viable.

items.question: Can I study part-time?
items.answer: The MPA track offers flexible and evening scheduling for working professionals. The MPP and MS in Data & Governance are full-time cohort programs.

items.question: Where do graduates work?
items.answer: Across all levels of government, nonprofit organizations, think tanks, and the fast-growing public-sector data field. About 90% of graduates are placed within six months of completing the program.
